newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Agouron profit targets lifted.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Agouron profit targets lifted.

text.p: Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Robert LeBoyer said he expects Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc to earn even more in the future than he had expected after a very strong response to the company's Viracept product in the fiscal fourth quarter
-- He raised 1998 profit estimates to $0.80 a share from $0.55. He lifted his near-term price target to $110 from $100 and his long-term target to $125 from $110 (on a pre-split basis).
-- Late on Thursday the company posted operating earnings of $0.17 a share compared with a loss of $0.17 last year and set a two-for-one stock split.
-- The stock rose 5-1/4 to 101 in the first minutes of trading and touched a new 52-week high of 103.

-- LeBoyer said the earnings, fueled by a strong jump in revenues, were well past his estimates. "They had an operating profit -- I wasn't expecting that until the second quarter next year. With the strong revenue and the improvment in margins, everything clicked all at once," he told Reuters.

-- "It was strong sales, an increase in demand, strong margins, growth of the market, a stock split, and no planned offerings in the next year. That's almost everything on my Christmas list," LeBoyer said.

-- He said the quarter had been under close scrutiny because it was the first full quarter of sales of Viracept, a protease inhibitor used in combination with other drugs to fight the HIV virus. The sales number is even more important, he said, because patients use the drug continually, so there are likely to be strong repeat sales.
-- Agouron also said it is seeing increasing demand for the drug, he said.
-- "Here was a company with no marketing experience and no drugs on the market going head-to-head against Merck and Co Inc. And they did it.
-- Agouron spokeswoman Donna Nichols said the company was up late fielding calls at its headquarters in La Jolla, California about the strong earnings.
"We were on the phone non-stop; we didn't even have time for champagne last night. But we deserve some," she said.
